rationale_summary: Renewed US-Iran strikes and Strait of Hormuz incidents drove crude sharply higher while rising yields (10y near 4.79%, 66% implied odds of a September Fed hike) pressured equities for a third straight session. Gold and silver fell hard despite escalating geopolitical risk and prior strong uptrends, which looks like a temporary rate-driven overreaction given the live safe-haven catalyst set (CPI Sept 11, PPI Sept 10, payrolls Sept 4) inside the window.
portfolio_rationale: Gold and silver combined strong prior relative trends with sharp one-week selloffs driven by rate repricing, while live Middle East escalation, Hormuz shipping risk, and a heavy inflation-data calendar inside the window give clear reversal catalysts; both are labeled overreaction with 55%+ beat odds. Oil ranks third on supported geopolitical continuation but is intentionally ineligible under the deterministic rule, so its slot defaults to SPY, limiting concentration.
key_risks: Rapid Middle East de-escalation would reverse oil gains and remove the safe-haven bid for gold and silver; Hot CPI/PPI or strong payrolls could push real yields higher, extending the precious-metals drawdown; A confirmed September Fed hike repricing could hit all high-beta assets and drag SPY-relative comparisons; Silver's 40% volatility makes the one-week outcome distribution very wide

rationale_summary: Rates are rising with a 66% implied probability of a September hike, inflation is re-accelerating (CPI 3.4%, PCE 3.7%, euro-area 3.3%), and oil has spiked on Strait of Hormuz disruption. Equities fell three sessions in a row with only 25% of assets positive over five days, while the prior month was broadly positive. That mix argues for a partial unwind of the sharp precious-metals flush (silver -7.7%, gold -5.8% in a week against a strongly positive prior trend and no fundamental change) and against chasing the oil/Taiwan momentum into OPEC+ and heavy macro prints. Cross-sectional dispersion of 2.75% is elevated, so selective reversal beats broad beta.
portfolio_rationale: The clearest mispricing is the one-week precious-metals flush against a strong prior trend with no offsetting fundamental change: inflation is re-accelerating and geopolitical risk is live, so silver and gold get the reversal nod. Materials adds a lower-volatility quality pullback with expansionary manufacturing support. Recent momentum leaders oil and Taiwan are ranked as no-edge continuation because their move is event-driven and faces OPEC+ and payroll catalysts inside the window.
key_risks: A hawkish September repricing after ADP, payrolls, and CPI could push real yields higher and extend the gold and silver decline.; OPEC+ supply news or Hormuz de-escalation could reverse the energy shock and drag broad commodity and materials sentiment.; Silver's 40% volatility means a single adverse session can dominate the one-week excess return.; Broad equity beta rebound would let SPY outperform low-beta and defensive commodity positions.; Only four scoring sessions plus a holiday-shortened week reduces the chance mean reversion completes.

Short-horizon breadth is weak (about 25% of assets positive over 5 sessions) but 21-session breadth remains majority-positive, so the week is mixed continuation in energy versus pullback/reversal tests in metals and cyclicals.
portfolio_rationale: The only slate names that combine a genuine recent overshoot with at least a modest chance of beating SPY are silver, gold, and materials after sharp pullbacks from strong prior trends. Oil has the strongest narrative but is already extended, while high-beta continuation names (Taiwan, crypto, momentum) and weak consumer/industrial prints do not clear a one-week excess-return bar versus SPY into payrolls and CPI.
key_risks: September 4 Employment Situation and September 11 CPI can extend the equity and duration selloff, dragging even oversold cyclicals.; Hormuz/oil news and the September 6 OPEC+ meeting can reverse oil or further strengthen the dollar, delaying a metals bounce.; Silver and gold 21s volatilities near 30–40% can produce large negative excess versus SPY even if the overreaction thesis is directionally right.

rationale_summary: High cross-sectional dispersion, weak equity breadth, rising yields, and an oil-driven inflation shock favor selective pullback reversals over broad risk taking; major labor and inflation releases create substantial one-week event risk.
